task.title: Renaming a status onto a retired name silently re-points the retirement chain
task.description:
Found during the PR #92 adversarial review, and verified PRE-EXISTING on main (the CLI status rename does the same thing; the web PATCH merely inherits it).

Repro: retire a status (e.g. status delete review3 --into backlog), then rename a live status onto the retired name (status rename ready review3). The command succeeds, and the whole alias chain that used to resolve through review3 into backlog is re-pointed at the renamed column. Stored task statuses that previously resolved to backlog now resolve to the new review3 -- a silent change of where historical statuses land, with no conflict or warning surfaced to the author.

Open design question: should renaming onto a retired name (a) be refused with guidance (the name is burdened with history; pick another), (b) be allowed with a loud warning naming how many stored statuses re-resolve, or (c) stay as-is with documentation? The correct-on-touch decay means long-lived projects shrink the exposure over time, which may argue for (b).

Evidence: two-binary verification in the PR #92 review record (rename onto retired name returns success on both main and the PR branch, chain re-pointed identically).
